about: The veil candidate's cast and trigger rules with the attack left to Forge (no attack policy), for a side-by-side run on the same tables. Only the playbook object is read.

playbook.notes: Deadly Disguise (Kaust, Eyes of the Glade: creatures cast face down, manifested and cloaked, then turned face up for their triggers). Stock Forge does cast face down (3.8 a game in the audit) and turns some face up, but leaves 67% of its mana unspent, sits on Mirror Entity (flagged never-cast), never taps Panoptic Projektor or Krosan Verge and is late with Kaust in a quarter of games. Rules: ramp first (Wild Growth is flagged never-cast), Kaust at once, the face-down engines (Obscuring Aether, flagged; Projektor, Trail of Mystery, Ugin's Mastery, Veiled Ascension, Bestiary, Scroll of Fate, Mastery of the Unseen), Projektor tapped whenever a morph or disguise card is in hand, the creature payoffs, then the morph/disguise cards: a play rule casts the face-up spell when it is affordable and the face-down one otherwise (the rule cannot choose), so the expensive ones go down face down and the two-mana ones face up. Scroll of Fate and Krosan Verge used when untapped; Mirror Entity for all the mana in the first main phase with three attackers; Mastery of the Unseen as the mana sink after combat (library >= 20). Optional triggers taken: Trail of Mystery's land, Bestiary's draw (library guarded), Ugin's Mastery's free turn-up, Imperial Hellkite's dragon, Deathmist Raptor, Veiled Ascension's cloak, Yedora, Broodhatch, Temur War Shaman, Root Elemental. Turning a face-down creature up is a static special action in Forge (ST$ SetState, not an activated ability), so no rule can do it, and Kaust's own ability works only on an attacking creature, outside the rules' main phases: both stay Forge's. Answers left to Forge. Go-wide attack as the batch's default.
